instruction: Draw a circle interactively using mouse in GraphWPF. Press and hold mouse button to draw circles with random colors.
Draw multiple mathematical functions (x*sin(x), sin, cos, exp) using GraphABC with transparent brush.
Draw mathematical functions in different scaled rectangles using GraphABC. Implement Scale and Move extension methods for Rectangle.
Draw multiple function graphs in different window quadrants using GraphWPF: sin(4x)+cos(3x), x², exp(x), and x*cos(2x-1).
Generate and display a pixel matrix with calculated RGB colors using GraphWPF, then measure drawing performance.
Draw random points using Turtle library. Generate arrays of random coordinates and plot them.
Create parametric trajectory functions and duplicate 3D objects along a spiral path using Graph3D.
Demonstrate basic operations with dynamic arrays in PascalABC.NET: creation, sorting, reversing, resizing, and searching.
Create and display a dynamic array of random integers using SetLength and foreach loop.
Demonstrate that dynamic array assignment creates references, not copies. Show how modifying one array affects another.
Show how SetLength preserves existing elements when resizing a dynamic array.
Demonstrate passing dynamic arrays as parameters. Show when to use var parameter for array creation.
Demonstrate common dynamic array errors: accessing array without memory allocation and index out of bounds.
Convert number to digits in base 2 and back using School library in PascalABC.NET.
Use div and mod operations to extract last digit and remove last digit from a number, and check if number is even.
Reverse the digits of a number using div and mod operations in PascalABC.NET.
Use Drawman library to draw simple geometric shapes. Move to point, draw line, and return to origin.
Download a file from web using System.Net.WebClient and execute it in PascalABC.NET.
Generate Dragon Curve fractal using GraphABC and Utils libraries in PascalABC.NET with performance measurement.
